# Security KB Articles — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Security KB Articles. Run status: COMPLETED.

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB binaries bind to localhost by default. Flare explains that a container binding to all interfaces becomes externally reachable only when networking and port publication expose it; internet exposure must be assessed from the deployment configuration. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-hardening/ · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://flare.io/learn/resources/blog/mongodb-ransom
- [statement] For Atlas OneLogin LDAP troubleshooting, MongoDB recommends checking whether ldapsearch returns the expected user DNs when authentication succeeds but authorization fails, and allowing the troubleshooting host in the LDAP service IP access list. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-ldaps-onelogin.md
- [statement] MongoDB security operations guidance includes reviewing product CVEs, applying upgrades, reviewing network-rule changes, and auditing user privileges; hardening is an ongoing process. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use TLS for client and inter-node traffic. Protect stored data with database encryption or appropriate operating-system or storage encryption. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Flare reported on January 26, 2026 that its internet-exposed, unauthenticated MongoDB honeypots received ransom notes within days. Its observed extortion pattern relied on unrestricted database access rather than an advanced exploit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-26) — https://flare.io/learn/resources/blog/mongodb-ransom
- [statement] The Atlas OneLogin integration guide concerns database users rather than Atlas administrative users. Security troubleshooting must identify which identity and access layer is failing. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-ldaps-onelogin.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB security guidance calls for enforced authentication, role-based authorization, and separate application or person identities with only the privileges each needs. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/
- [statement] TLS protects client and cluster communication; storage encryption and application-side field encryption address different data exposure boundaries. Security articles should explain these controls separately. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/
- [statement] Restrict database traffic to trusted clients using private networks and firewall or security-group rules; enabling authentication does not replace network restrictions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://flare.io/learn/resources/blog/mongodb-ransom, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/security-hardening/, https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/
- [statement] Flare distinguished more than 200,000 publicly discoverable MongoDB servers from approximately 3,100 without access restrictions; it found 1,416 wiped instances with ransom notes in the latter group. These are study observations, not a current global inventory. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-26) — https://flare.io/learn/resources/blog/mongodb-ransom
- [statement] In a January 2021 MongoDB staff explanation, security.transitionToAuth permits unauthenticated access and does not enforce authorization. Completing the transition requires removing that setting; verify the procedure against the deployed server version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2021-01-21) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/incrementally-enabling-authentication/14556 · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/upgrading-from-mongodb-2-4-to-4-4/12390/4
- [statement] MongoDB closed its December 2023 corporate-systems incident investigation in January 2024 and reported no evidence of unauthorized Atlas cluster access. Its notices distinguish exposed customer contact/account metadata from customer databases. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-01-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/mongodb-security-bulletins/archive
- [statement] The 2019 DIMAQS paper discusses MongoDB ransomware as motivation but evaluates its query-sequence detection proof of concept on MySQL; its reported detection results do not establish a validated MongoDB defense. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06775
- [statement] Review security logs and privileges regularly, and keep MongoDB and its host patched; these are ongoing operational controls. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/security-checklist.md · keywords: Security KB Articles · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/
- [statement] A ransom note does not demonstrate recoverability: Flare describes data deletion and warns that attackers may not possess data they promise to return. (low confidence) — https://flare.io/learn/resources/blog/mongodb-ransom
- [statement] For CVE-2025-14847, MongoDB reports completing Atlas fleet patching on December 18, 2025 and publishing patched self-managed builds. This historical provider action does not establish that an individual self-managed deployment is patched. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-29) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/news/mongodb-server-security-update-december-2025
